text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to begin assessing your newborn's respiratory distress, please tell me how many hours old the baby is and describe exactly when these breathing difficulties started.

text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the history of preterm birth (32 weeks) and maternal gestational diabetes, and knowing the distress began shortly after birth, I need to know if the baby has a history of apnea or cyanosis, and has a chest X-ray been performed yet? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical presentation of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a 32-week preterm infant born via C-section is classic for RDS.
